newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa end narrowly mixed, stays clear of 899.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa end narrowly mixed, stays clear of 899.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended mixed on Friday and March managed to stay clear of the sensitive 899 stg, but turnover was meagre.
Benchmark March futures closed two stg higher at 908 stg a tonne after trading down to a low of 900. It was pressured early on by buffer stock sales by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO).
"All you have seen today is a bit of liquidation ahead of the holiday period. A lot of traders will be away next week," said one trader.
But trade buying at the lows underpinned the market at the close.
The day's volume totalled 2,557 lots, mostly on the March.

Technical analysts said this week's nine-month low of 899 continued to be a threat after the market seemed to lose stamina on the possibility of a sustained recovery. Upside attempts could be capped at around 915 stg for March.
"We'll probably break 899 but not break down," said one trader.

But some analysts reckoned prices have bottomed out. Brokers GNI said: "GNI remain confident that prices are at their bottom and will soon start to recover -- aided by a supply deficit much larger than the current consensus.".
